page: Microsoft Azure E4pds_v5 is an ARM-based memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Ampere Altra processor with ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 cores operating at 3.0 GHz. The instance provisions 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, coupled with 32 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. A 161 GB local SSD is bundled directly with the instance under Microsoft Hyper-V, providing high-speed scratch space alongside support for premium remote storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent baseline compute and memory subsystem capabilities. While stress-ng CPU tests and PassMark database operations place the instance in the middle tier, Geekbench compute metrics and PassMark overall scores measure in lower percentiles compared across varied x86 architectures. Large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidths record stable mid-tier marks at 48.18 GB/sec and 27.09 GB/sec respectively, whereas single-core performance and cryptographic operations show conservative output.

From an infrastructure perspective, the dedicated-core ARM architecture delivers predictable core isolation without thread contention. This profile offers cost-efficient RAM density for deployments that do not require x86-specific instruction sets such as AVX-512. The instance is well-matched for intermediate relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, containerized microservices, and general ARM64 development environments requiring substantial memory headroom and fast local temporary storage.
description: Microsoft Azure E4pds_v5 is an ARM64 memory-optimized virtual machine running on an Ampere Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 3.0 GHz. It features 4 dedicated physical vCPUs without multithreading, 32 GB of RAM (8 GB per vCPU), and a bundled 161 GB local SSD for high-speed scratch storage. Benchmarks show balanced medium-tier performance in multi-core stress testing, uncached memory bandwidth, and database transaction workloads, alongside lower throughput on compute-heavy operations like ray tracing and encryption. Without hardware GPU acceleration or x86 instruction sets, the architecture provides predictable dedicated core isolation and cost-efficient memory density. The instance serves intermediate caching tiers, relational database engines, ARM software builds, and memory-dependent enterprise microservices needing rapid local disk access.
